clue.text: Pole or pipe down at the back

parts.note: pipe down is a demand for quiet, as is sh
aft is the nautical word for at or towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone is told to choose a pole or else keep quiet at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' looks like a second object beside the pole, but 'pipe down' is one phrase, a request for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long rod such as the handle of a spear or a spade.

clue.text: Class item in series four, perhaps?

parts.note: a series of things is a set of them
four is an example of a square number, being two times two

explanation.surface: A school lesson might feature in the fourth series of a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests social rank or a TV series; it is the geometry classroom, where this drawing triangle lives. 'perhaps' flags four as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a triangular drawing instrument found in a school geometry lesson.

clue.text: Nation in pursuit of war, so unfortunately one having a row

indicators.note: in pursuit of places the nation behind the other piece, following it
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of the two words before it are disordered

parts.note: Oman is a nation on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A country bent on war ends up with someone quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' makes OARSW, and 'in pursuit of' sets the country behind it. 'having a row' reads as an argument but means propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a female rower is someone who has a row in the boating sense.

clue.text: Courts detailing one of their procedures?

indicators.note: read as de-tailing, it removes the tail, the last letter, of the phrase that follows

parts.note: a trial is one of the procedures of law courts

explanation.surface: Law courts set out the particulars of one of their processes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailing' is read as de-tailing: A TRIAL loses its final L. The courts of the definition are open halls, not the legal ones the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the architectural sense: open central halls or courtyards in buildings.

clue.text: Quality of sound marginally better initially, having blocked exhaust

indicators.note: having blocked says the two initials have lodged inside the other word, as a blockage sits inside a pipe

parts.note: to exhaust someone is to tire them

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A car sounds slightly nicer at first once its exhaust pipe has been stopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes M and B from 'marginally better', and 'having blocked' puts them inside TIRE. The exhaust is a verb, not the car part.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the distinctive tone colour of a voice or instrument.

clue.text: Hot diet? Cold!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap
to diet is to eat less

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the slimming meal is spicy and learns it is chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like two opposites; 'diet' is a verb, eat less, following the tap letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking any warmth.

clue.text: Scholar as postal worker?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a fellow whose job is delivering the mail

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a learned literary person, which taken literally also describes a chap who delivers mail.

clue.text: Saw three pigs cast aside

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters of the three words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a trio of hogs thrown to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast aside' reads as one phrase but splits: 'cast' is the anagram signal for SAW THREE PIGS, and 'aside' alone is the theatrical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a loud utterance on stage meant for the audience, supposedly unheard by other characters.

clue.text: A further, ridiculous, reclining little Cupid

parts.note: further means more, as in further help

indicators.note: reclining means lying back, so the piece beside it is laid backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, is slang for ridiculous or excessive

explanation.surface: Yet another silly cherub lounges about in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reclining' turns OTT into TTO. OTT is the abbreviation of 'over the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in art: a cherub or small figure of the love god.

clue.text: Doctor in Gounod opera not entirely celebrated

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the shortened opera
not entirely means the opera is not used whole and loses its last letter

parts.note: Faust is the best-known opera by the French composer Charles Gounod
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor appearing in a French opera is not fully acclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' at the front looks like an anagram signal; it is a plain medic placed by 'in' inside the opera, which 'not entirely' cuts to FAUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: widely known and renowned.

clue.text: Spill beans all round sort of shirt that's smart

indicators.note: all round wraps the first piece about the second

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police, spilling the beans
a T-shirt is a sort of shirt, giving the letter T

explanation.surface: Someone drops baked beans all over a rather stylish shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' puts SING about T. 'smart' looks like stylish but is the verb meaning to hurt sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to feel or cause a sharp burning pain.

clue.text: Taking part in duel, I'm in a temper — kill!

indicators.note: Taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A furious duellist urges himself on to finish his opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: to get rid of someone by murdering them.

clue.text: Getting to grips with shake when dancing, couple move it!

indicators.note: getting to grips with means the couple word grasps the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to couple is to mate, as animals do

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair of dancers learn the shake and get going on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when dancing' rearranges SHAKE into AKEHAS, which MATE holds because of 'Getting to grips with'. 'couple' is a verb here, not a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both are informal commands to hurry up.

clue.text: The sappers told you so!

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, RE, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers smugly point out that they warned you.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers, in Britain the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an exclamation of vindication when a prediction comes true.

clue.text: When the performance starts with some somersaults

indicators.note: somersaults are tumbles, so the letters of the two words before it tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A circus act opens with a few acrobatic tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaults' is the anagram signal, working as a verb on WITH SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: the hour at which an entertainment is due to begin.

clue.text: I am to punch a friend in the spleen

indicators.note: to punch is to drive into, so the contraction is driven into the other letters

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or companion
I am contracts to I'm, giving IM

explanation.surface: The speaker plans to hit a pal in the abdomen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to punch' drives the contraction into the friend phrase. The spleen is not the organ but ill temper, once thought to be seated there.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the figurative sense: bitterness and bad temper.

clue.text: Rock getting powerful tug, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a person who gives dependable support
a tug is a boat that tows, so a mighty one is whimsically a very strong puller

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a dependable supporter, and read differently a punning description of a mighty towing vessel.

clue.text: Total football's second sport

parts.note: a total is a sum

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Total football is only the second-favourite game.
explanation.walkthrough: Total football is a famous Dutch style of play, but the phrase splits: 'Total' is one piece and 'football's second' gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Japanese wrestling is one kind.

clue.text: Hollywood element, fifty in group, private

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group of people or things
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
one's own room is a private one

explanation.surface: A film-industry faction of fifty people keeps itself to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the Roman numeral inside the group only; the surface's secretive clique hides three separate pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname: the informal name for the American film industry's home.

clue.text: One of eight left Iraq after insult mishandled

indicators.note: something mishandled is badly managed, so the letters of the three words before it are disarranged

explanation.surface: One of eight diplomats walked out of Iraq when an affront was badly dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a departure or the letter L, but belongs to the definition: eight competitors remain at this stage. 'mishandled' rearranges IRAQ AFTER INSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: a competitor at the knockout stage when eight remain.

clue.text: You're on grass, after a little taste of ganja

indicators.note: after places the grass behind the other two pieces
a little taste of something is its first small bit, here the opening letter

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are smoking weed after a small sample of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little taste of' takes the G of ganja, and 'after' puts REED behind A G. The grass is a plant, not the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both are said to accept a bet or a deal.

clue.text: Pass South Pole, going north, then east

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the two pieces before it are written backwards

parts.note: a pale is a pointed stake or pole in a fence

explanation.surface: An explorer goes by the bottom of the world, heads up and then turns right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns S PALE into ELAPS. The South Pole splits into a compass point and a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what time does as it goes by.

clue.text: Floating, with and without a crew?

parts.note: an eight is the crew of a rowing boat with eight oars
less means without, as in a year less a day

explanation.surface: A boat drifts along, sometimes manned and sometimes not.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order with, a crew, without. An eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an astronaut in orbit has no apparent heaviness and drifts freely.

clue.text: Happy to see with it

parts.note: someone who is cheerful is said to be up, the opposite of down
to see someone is to date them romantically

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to witness something along with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' is not a tag on the sentence but the definition, the old slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean modern and fashionable.

clue.text: Talk about river only as lake

indicators.note: about wraps the talk word round the river's letter

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
R is the map abbreviation for river
mere means only, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of a river as though it were just a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside GAS. This lake is in the English Lake District, where Wordsworth lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a named body of water in the English Lake District.

clue.text: Wood nymph's heart, a fragrant thing

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood used for models

indicators.note: heart picks the central letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A forest spirit's heart is a sweet-smelling thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood nymph' reads as one creature but splits: 'Wood' is the timber and 'heart' takes the M from the middle of nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an aromatic resin or soothing ointment.

clue.text: Help certainly required to climb over head of koala bear

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the climbing pieces above the last letter
in a down clue climbing is going up, so the two pieces before it are written upwards

parts.note: aid means help
OK is said for certainly, as a reply of assent

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A koala will surely need a hand to clamber over its own head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to climb' makes KODIA, which sits 'over' the letter that 'head of' picks. 'koala bear' splits: only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a very large brown one from an Alaskan island.

clue.text: Magnificent penalty

definitions.meaning: splendid or excellent, as an adjective
a sum of money paid as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for splendid, and a noun for money paid as punishment.
